items.reason: The first destination calendar can be undefined, and accessing its integration crashes Meet booking creation instead of triggering the fallback.
updateLocation saves routing fields from updateEvent results that do not contain them, losing the calendar and credential association.
The hangout-link patch receives an undefined calendarId when no destination matches because only the insert applies the primary-calendar fallback.
The fallback searches for the already-falsy externalCalendarId, so updateEvent and deleteEvent fail to use the configured destination calendar.
The optional push discards secondary hosts' destination calendars when the organizer's destinationCalendar is null.
Office365 and Lark select the first destination instead of the destination belonging to the credential creating the event.
An undefined first destination calendar is dereferenced during the Meet fallback, crashing event creation.
The unguarded integration access throws when the destination calendar array is empty, preventing the Cal Video fallback.
The update/delete fallback compares destination external IDs against the absent externalCalendarId, losing the configured destination.
Reading integration from an undefined first destination calendar crashes Meet bookings with no destination.
The fallback predicate uses the same falsy externalCalendarId that selected the fallback branch, so it cannot recover the destination calendar.
Non-calendar references lose result.credentialId, preventing later operations from resolving the video credential.
It identifies the same unguarded integration access on a potentially undefined first destination calendar in EventManager.

It identifies the legacy createAllCalendarEvents branch omitting externalId and requests passing it through. That fixes the omission in issue #15 despite the comment's different explanation of its consequence.
The unused message variable in a catch block is a separate dead-code finding that no golden-set issue describes.
